date.quote: The Petitioner assails the Show Cause Notice dated 29.07.2024 issued by the Directorate General of GST Intelligence, Delhi Zonal Unit [„DGGI/DZU‟] under Sections 74 and 122 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 [„CGST Act‟], read with Section 20 of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 [„IGST Act‟].
The present judgment shall accordingly proceed on the basis that the impugned Order-in-Original was passed on 31.01.2025.

In the course of the investigation, searches were conducted on 11.09.2019 and 18.10.2019, and statements of Shri Parag Garg, stated to be a Director of the Petitioner, were recorded under Section 70 of the CGST Act.
The DGGI Show Cause Notice dated 29.07.2024 was issued under Section 74 of the CGST Act and covers the period from FY 2017-18 (July onwards) to FY 2019-20.
A corrigendum was thereafter issued on 23.12.2024.
On 31.01.2025, the competent adjudicating authority passed Order-in-Original No. 73/SPP/ADC/CGST/DSC/2024-25 pursuant to the Show Cause Notice dated 29.07.2024.

document_contents.quote: The said Show Cause Notice proposed, inter alia, recovery of ITC aggregating to Rs.7,81,78,980/-, comprising IGST of Rs.4,46,05,885/-, CGST of Rs.1,67,86,547/- and SGST of Rs.1,67,86,547/-, along with applicable interest and penalties.

The proceedings initiated by the DGGI, on the other hand, arise out of an investigation into alleged fraudulent availment of ITC on the basis of invoices issued by non-existent and fictitious entities and the alleged utilisation of such ITC towards payment of IGST on exports and consequential availment of IGST refunds.
By the said order, the demand of Rs.7,81,78,980/- was confirmed under Section 74(9) of the CGST Act read with the relevant provisions of the DGST Act and the IGST Act, along with applicable interest.

defects_argued.quote: Consequently, the mere fact that the Show Cause Notice dated 29.07.2024 covers more than one financial year cannot, by itself, render the notice without jurisdiction.
It was further submitted that the proceedings initiated by the DGGI also concern alleged wrongful availment and utilisation of ITC for substantially the same period.

outcome.quote: In view of the aforesaid discussion, the present Writ Petition is dismissed.
